description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (35 = 5 × 7 means 35 is 5 times as many as 7), and represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.
skill list: U3 Multiplicative Comparisons

description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.
skill list: U3 Multiplicative Comparisons; U4 Interpreting Remainders in Word Problems

description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted; represent them with equations with a letter for the unknown; assess reasonableness using mental computation and estimation, including rounding.
skill list: U2 Estimating Sums and Differences; U2 Addition and Subtraction Word Problems; U3 Estimating Products and Multiplication Word Problems; U4 Interpreting Remainders in Word Problems; U10 Multi-Step Word Problems; U10 Equations and Reasonable Answers

description: (Massachusetts) Know multiplication facts and related division facts through 12 × 12.
skill list: U3 Multiplying by Multiples of 10, 100, and 1,000; U4 Division Facts and Patterns

description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100; recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors; determine whether a whole number is a multiple of a given one-digit number; determine whether a whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.
skill list: U5 Factors and Factor Pairs; U5 Multiples; U5 Prime and Composite Numbers

description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule; identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
skill list: U5 Number Patterns and Rules; U5 Shape Patterns and Pattern Features

description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
skill list: U1 Place Value to One Million

description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form; compare two multi-digit numbers using >, =, and < symbols.
skill list: U1 Reading and Writing Multi-Digit Numbers; U1 Comparing and Ordering Whole Numbers

description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
skill list: U1 Rounding Whole Numbers; U2 Estimating Sums and Differences

description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
skill list: U2 Adding Multi-Digit Whole Numbers; U2 Subtracting Multi-Digit Whole Numbers; U2 Subtracting Across Zeros; U2 Addition and Subtraction Word Problems

description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations; illustrate and explain with equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
skill list: U3 Multiplying by Multiples of 10, 100, and 1,000; U3 Multiplying by One-Digit Numbers; U3 Multiplying Two-Digit Numbers; U3 Estimating Products and Multiplication Word Problems

description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division; illustrate and explain with equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
skill list: U4 Division Facts and Patterns; U4 Dividing with Models and Partial Quotients; U4 Dividing by One-Digit Divisors; U4 Division with Remainders

description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models; use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.
skill list: U6 Understanding Equivalent Fractions; U6 Generating Equivalent Fractions

description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2; record the results with >, =, or <.
skill list: U6 Comparing Fractions with Common Denominators or Numerators; U6 Comparing Fractions with Benchmarks; U6 Ordering Fractions

description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
skill list: U7 Decomposing Fractions; U7 Adding and Subtracting Fractions with Like Denominators

description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation.
skill list: U7 Decomposing Fractions

description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.
skill list: U7 Adding and Subtracting Mixed Numbers

description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators.
skill list: U7 Adding and Subtracting Fractions with Like Denominators; U7 Adding and Subtracting Mixed Numbers

description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
skill list: U7 Multiplying a Fraction by a Whole Number

description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
skill list: U7 Multiplying a Fraction by a Whole Number

description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number.
skill list: U7 Multiplying a Fraction by a Whole Number

description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.
skill list: U7 Tenths and Hundredths as Fractions and Decimals

description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
skill list: U7 Tenths and Hundredths as Fractions and Decimals

description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size; record the results with >, =, or <.
skill list: U7 Comparing Decimals

description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units (km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz; l, ml; hr, min, sec); express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit; record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.
skill list: U8 Customary Units and Conversions; U8 Metric Units and Conversions; U8 Time and Elapsed Time

description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals; represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams.
skill list: U8 Time and Elapsed Time; U8 Measurement and Money Word Problems

description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and mathematical problems.
skill list: U8 Area and Perimeter of Rectangles

description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8); solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
skill list: U10 Reading and Making Line Plots; U10 Solving Problems with Line Plots

description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays; an angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a one-degree angle.
skill list: U9 Measuring Angles

description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.
skill list: U9 Measuring Angles

description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor; sketch angles of specified measure.
skill list: U9 Measuring Angles

description: Recognize angle measure as additive; solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems.
skill list: U9 Adding and Subtracting Angle Measures

description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines; identify these in two-dimensional figures.
skill list: U9 Points, Lines, Rays, and Angles

description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size; recognize right triangles as a category.
skill list: U9 Classifying Triangles and Quadrilaterals

description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts; identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
skill list: U9 Lines of Symmetry
